newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Extremists disrupt Austrian war crimes exhibition.
newsitem.headline: Extremists disrupt Austrian war crimes exhibition.

text.p: Two suspected far-right extremists were arrested in southern Austria on Tuesday after they stormed an exhibition on Nazi war crimes and threatened over 200 visiting schoolchildren, the exhibition's organiser said.

The two men in their 30s attempted to clear visitors from the gallery in Klagenfurt, southern Austria, and disrupt an exhibition on the World War Two crimes of Adolf Hitler's Wehrmacht, according to organiser Birgit Hebein.
"Leave the room immediately...You remain at your own risk," they screamed as they scattered a white powder, later identified as salt.
They also tried to distribute leaflets and blasted the exhibition as a "public incitement".
When it became clear that the two were not armed, exhibition visitors formed a circle around them and waited for the police to arrive, Hebein said.

Austrian news agency APA said it had earlier received a faxed letter from the two men. In it they demanded one billion dollars from the exhibition organisers to make good the insult to those who suffered and died in World War Two.
The letter ended with the words: "No more anti-fascism", APA said.
The incident came hot on the heels of an Austrian government warning of a possible far-right bomb campaign ahead of Vienna state elections and European parliamentary elections on October 13.
